To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a fast one-step bio-synthesis of silver nanoparticles is possible using peanut skin extract; 2) the nanoparticles thus produced show a significant ferro-magnetic behavior and 3) the prepared nanoparticles are suitable for iodide ion sensing.
silver nanoparticles prepared by peanut skin extract are diamagnetic and show anion sensing property.

1) the silver nanoparticles prepared by peanut skin extract are ferromagnetic in nature and the ferromagnetic moment decays exponentially with γ-radiation exposure, 2) the nanoparticles exhibit selective anion sensing behavior towards iodide anions.

the synthesis of silver nanoparticles using peanut skin extract and the study of their structural, magnetic, optical, catalytic and anion sensing properties.
the synthesis of Ag-nanoparticle by an ecofriendly route, their structural and magnetic characterizations and their application in the sensing of iodide ions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
silver nanoparticles synthesized by peanut polyphenol extract are ferromagnetic in nature and are suitable for sensing anions.

The main takeaway from our work is that
silver nanoparticles can be prepared in situ in the presence of polyphenol, which is an abundant and easily accessible material, and can be used to sense anions at trace concentration.
the polyphenols present in the peanut skin extract are responsible for reduction of Ag+ and stabilization of the nanoparticles.
the silver nanoparticles thus produced can be used for both anion sensing and magnetic application.
